message.reasoning_content:
We need to determine statutory charges based on Chinese criminal law. Facts: bribery (giving kickbacks to a hospital department head). The defendant supplied medical consumables, gave kickbacks to the head of orthopedics department, total 790,000 yuan. This is a case of bribery of a public official (the department head likely a public servant). Under Chinese Criminal Law, article 385 (bribery of public officials) or article 389 (unit bribery). Also possibly "非法经营罪"? But main is "受贿罪" is for officials receiving bribes; "行贿罪" is for giving bribes. So charge: 行贿罪 (bribery). Also could be "商业贿赂罪"? Actually Chinese law has "行贿罪" (giving bribes) and "商业贿赂罪" is a separate provision for business bribery (Article 389). The fact: a private individual gives bribes to a public official to secure business. That's "行贿罪". Also could be "非法经营罪"? No.

Thus answer: [罪名]行贿罪<eoa>

But they ask "statutory charge(s)" maybe include "行贿罪" and "非法经营罪"? The text says "已触犯《中华人民共和国刑法》××××、××××之规定，应以××追究其刑事责任". They omitted article numbers. Likely article 385 (行贿罪) and article 389 (单位行贿罪) if the entity is a unit. But the defendant is an individual. So just 行贿罪.

Thus final answer: [罪名]行贿罪<eoa>
